source.public_versification_note: English Genesis 31:55 is bound to Hebrew Gen 32:1, whose original XML record includes the note KJV:Gen.31.55.

key_decisions.decision: Clarify the broad Hebrew son relationship from the genealogy while retaining Laban and Nahor rather than silently omitting the ancestry.
Choose gentle for the ambiguous rakkot without implying weak eyesight; preserve the explicit description of Rachel’s form and appearance.
Render the sexual euphemism plainly in Jacob’s direct request while retaining wife and completion of service.
Make Zilpah’s enslaved status and transfer between Laban and Leah explicit rather than presenting voluntary domestic employment.
Interpret the seven as the bridal week from the immediate fulfillment in verse 28; retain the collective we and further labor demand.
Make Bilhah’s enslaved status and transfer explicit, parallel to Zilpah in verse 24.
Retain the strong source word hated rather than reducing Leah’s condition to a neutral comparison; render barrenness as inability without blame.
Preserve attached as the name wordplay and the passive naming form, whose namer is not specified.
